## 0. Setup directory
### 0.1 Setup genome name and directory
```{r setup, include=FALSE}
genomename1a <- 'tair10_original'
genomename2a <- 'rice_original'
genomename3a <- 'maize_original'
genomename4a <- 'dm6_original'
genomename5a <- 'danio_original'

genomename1b <- 'tair10_simulated'
short_gname1b <- 'tair10_run7'
genomename2b <- 'rice_simulated'
short_gname2b <- 'rice'
genomename3b <- 'maize_simulated'
short_gname3b <- 'maize_run3'
genomename4b <- 'dm6_simulated'
short_gname4b <- 'dm6'
genomename5b <- 'danio_simulated'
short_gname5b <- 'danio'

WRK <- "/workspace/cflthc/script"
setwd(WRK)
SIM1 <- file.path(WRK, "TEgenomeSimulator_pub/output/tair10/output/TEgenomeSimulator_tair10_run7_result/")
SIM2 <- file.path(WRK, "TEgenomeSimulator_pub/output/TEgenomeSimulator_rice_result/")
SIM3 <- file.path(WRK, "TEgenomeSimulator_pub/output/TEgenomeSimulator_maize_run3_result/")
SIM4 <- file.path(WRK, "TEgenomeSimulator_pub/output/TEgenomeSimulator_dm6_result/")
SIM5 <- file.path(WRK, "TEgenomeSimulator_pub/output/TEgenomeSimulator_danio_result/")

OUT <- file.path(WRK, "TEgenomeSimulator_publication_code/output/corr_identity_integrity/")
dir.create(file.path(OUT), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir=OUT)
```


## 1. tair10
### 1.1 original genome
#### 1.1.1 load files
```{r, load_files_ori_tair10, include=FALSE}
rmout1 <- read.table(paste0(SIM1, 'processed_output.temp'), header = T, sep = '\t', comment.char = "")
rmout1 <- rmout1 |> mutate(div = as.numeric(1 - identity), itg = as.numeric(length_ratio)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(superfamily = gsub("auto", "", superfamily)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(superfamily = gsub("nona", "", superfamily)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(superfamily = gsub("DNA\\/Helitron", "RC\\/Helitron", superfamily)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(superfamily = gsub("DNA\\/CMC.*", "DNA\\/CACTA", superfamily)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(superfamily = gsub("DNA\\/MULE.*", "DNA\\/MULE", superfamily)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(superfamily = gsub("DNA\\/MuDR.*", "DNA\\/MULE", superfamily)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(superfamily = gsub("DNA\\/PIF-Harbinger", "DNA\\/Harbinger", superfamily)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(superfamily = gsub("DNA\\/TcMar.*", "DNA\\/Mariner", superfamily)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(superfamily = gsub("DNA\\/hAT.*", "DNA\\/hAT", superfamily)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(superfamily = gsub("LTR\\/Gypsy", "LTR\\/Ty3", superfamily)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(superfamily = gsub("DNA$", "DNA\\/unknown", superfamily)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(itg = if_else(itg > 1, 1, itg))
rmtbl1 <- paste0(SIM1, "repeatmasker/GCF_000001735.4_TAIR10.1_genomic.fna.tbl")
```

## 3. Analysis 1: correlation between identity and integrity — real vs. mode-2 simulated

For each of the five validation genomes, compute the Pearson and Spearman correlation between
TE loci divergence (1 - identity) and integrity, separately for (a) the real/original genome
(empirical, from RepeatMasker output) and (b) the mode-2 simulated digital replica. Loci with
missing or out-of-range (itg < 0) integrity values are excluded, consistent with the filtering
already used for the distribution plots above.

```{r, corr_analysis1_compute, echo=FALSE}
source(file.path(WRK, "TEgenomeSimulator_publication_code/script/functions.R"))
genomes <- c("tair10", "rice", "maize", "dm6", "danio")
ori_list <- list(rmout1, rmout2, rmout3, rmout4, rmout5)
sim_list <- list(breakdown1, breakdown2, breakdown3, breakdown4, breakdown5)

corr_summary <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(genomes), function(i){
  ori_df <- ori_list[[i]] |> dplyr::filter(itg >= 0)
  sim_df <- sim_list[[i]] |> dplyr::filter(div >= 0, itg >= 0)
  rbind(
    compute_corr_identity_integrity(ori_df, genomes[i], "Real (original)"),
    compute_corr_identity_integrity(sim_df, genomes[i], "Mode 2 (simulated)")
  )
}))
rownames(corr_summary) <- NULL

write.csv(corr_summary, paste0(OUT, "corr_identity_integrity_summary.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r, corr_analysis1_table, echo=FALSE}
kable(corr_summary, digits = 3,
      caption = "Pearson and Spearman correlation between TE loci divergence and integrity: real (original) vs. mode-2 simulated (digital replica) genomes.")
```

### 3.1 Divergence vs. integrity, per species (real vs. mode-2 simulated)

One figure per genome, real vs. mode-2 simulated side by side. Because the real and simulated
loci counts for the same species are always close in magnitude (a matched pair), both panels
share one raw-count log10 fill scale, so the legend shows a genuine, comparable TE loci count.

```{r, corr_analysis1_plot_by_genome, echo=FALSE, fig.width = 8, fig.asp = .45, results = "asis"}
source(file.path(WRK, "TEgenomeSimulator_publication_code/script/functions.R"))
genome_plots <- vector("list", length(genomes))
names(genome_plots) <- genomes

for (i in seq_along(genomes)) {
  df_genome <- rbind(
    ori_list[[i]] |> dplyr::filter(itg >= 0) |>
      dplyr::transmute(div, itg, dataset = "Real (original)"),
    sim_list[[i]] |> dplyr::filter(div >= 0, itg >= 0) |>
      dplyr::transmute(div, itg, dataset = "Mode 2 (simulated)")
  )
  p <- plot_corr_identity_integrity_one_genome(df_genome, genomes[i])
  genome_plots[[genomes[i]]] <- p

  png(filename = paste0(OUT, "corr_identity_integrity_", genomes[i], ".png"), width = 8, height = 3.6, units = "in", res = 1200)
  print(p)
  while (!is.null(dev.list()))  dev.off()

  cat("\n\n#### ", genomes[i], "\n\n")
  print(p)
  cat("\n\nSaved file name: corr_identity_integrity_", genomes[i], ".png\n\n", sep = "")
}
```

## 4. Analysis 2: mode-1 correlation baseline ("by construction ~0")

Modes 0 and 1 both draw identity and integrity from independent distributions (Gaussian
identity, Beta integrity) at simulation time, so any identity-integrity correlation observed
under either mode is not designed in - it is the null baseline against which the real/mode-2
correlations in Analysis 1 should be judged. This section uses **mode 1 only**: the
`TEgenomeSimulator_tair10_ch1_m0_*` runs originally considered for the mode-0 baseline turned
out to have been simulated using a TE mutagenesis table (`TElib_sim_list_mode2.table`)
generated by mode 2, not mode 0's own independent draw, so they are not a valid mode-0 baseline
and are excluded. Since a genuine mode-0 run uses the same underlying identity/integrity
sampling model as mode 1, mode 1's result is representative of both. Data reused from the item
29 replicate-run work (no new simulation):

- **Mode 1**: the 4 Fig. 3D identity-SD scenarios x 5 reps each = 20 tair10 (whole-genome) simulations
  (`TEgenomeSimulator_tair10_sd_scenario{1-4}_rep{1-5}_result`), reported both pooled across all 20
  and per scenario (5 reps pooled per scenario), to check that the null correlation holds
  regardless of the identity-SD setting.

```{r, load_mode1, include=FALSE}
source(file.path(WRK, "TEgenomeSimulator_publication_code/script/functions.R"))
BASELINE_DIR <- file.path(WRK, "TEgenomeSimulator_publication_code/output/")

mode1_list <- list()
for (s in 1:4) {
  for (r in 1:5) {
    d <- file.path(BASELINE_DIR, paste0("TEgenomeSimulator_tair10_sd_scenario", s, "_rep", r, "_result/"))
    gff <- read.table(paste0(d, "tair10_sd_scenario", s, "_rep", r, "_repeat_annotation_out_final.gff"), header = F, sep = '\t', comment.char = "")
    mode1_list[[paste0("s", s, "_r", r)]] <- te_breakdown_sim_genome(gff) |> dplyr::mutate(scenario = s, rep = r)
  }
}
mode1_pooled <- do.call(rbind, mode1_list) |> dplyr::filter(div >= 0, itg >= 0)
```

```{r, corr_analysis2_compute, echo=FALSE}
mode1_summary <- rbind(
  compute_corr_identity_integrity(mode1_pooled, "tair10", "Mode 1 (pooled, 20 genomes)"),
  do.call(rbind, lapply(1:4, function(s){
    compute_corr_identity_integrity(
      mode1_pooled |> dplyr::filter(scenario == s),
      "tair10", paste0("Mode 1 (scenario ", s, ", pooled 5 reps)")
    )
  }))
)
rownames(mode1_summary) <- NULL

write.csv(mode1_summary, paste0(OUT, "corr_identity_integrity_mode1_baseline.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
kable(mode1_summary, digits = 3,
      caption = "Pearson and Spearman correlation between TE loci divergence and integrity in mode-1 simulated data, where identity and integrity are drawn independently by construction (representative of both modes 0 and 1).")
```

Saved file name: corr_identity_integrity_mode1_baseline.csv

## 5. Analysis 3: non-independence caveat and family-level robustness check

TE loci within a genome are not independent observations: loci belonging to the same TE family
share evolutionary history (a single ancestral insertion event, correlated copy number and age),
so the per-locus `cor.test()` results in Analyses 1-2 above have an effective sample size well
below the raw `n_loci` reported - the same non-independence issue already raised for the
Shannon-entropy/Wilcoxon analysis elsewhere in this revision (overlapping/non-independent
windows inflating apparent significance). Non-independence inflates the *p-value's* apparent
confidence, not the correlation coefficient itself, so the effect size and its confidence
interval - not the p-value - should be treated as the primary evidence from Analyses 1-2.

As a robustness check, each TE family is collapsed to its median divergence and median
integrity (one data point per family, regardless of how many loci it contains), and the same
Pearson/Spearman test is re-run on those family-level medians, real vs. mode-2, across all 5
species. If the family-level result agrees in sign and rough magnitude with the per-locus
result, that is evidence the per-locus correlation is not solely a within-family
pseudoreplication artefact.

```{r, corr_analysis3_compute, echo=FALSE}
source(file.path(WRK, "TEgenomeSimulator_publication_code/script/functions.R"))
corr_family_summary <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(genomes), function(i){
  ori_df <- ori_list[[i]] |> dplyr::filter(itg >= 0)
  sim_df <- sim_list[[i]] |> dplyr::filter(div >= 0, itg >= 0)
  rbind(
    compute_corr_identity_integrity_family(ori_df, genomes[i], "Real (original)"),
    compute_corr_identity_integrity_family(sim_df, genomes[i], "Mode 2 (simulated)")
  )
}))
rownames(corr_family_summary) <- NULL

write.csv(corr_family_summary, paste0(OUT, "corr_identity_integrity_family_level.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
kable(corr_family_summary, digits = 3,
      caption = "Family-level robustness check: Pearson/Spearman correlation between median divergence and median integrity per TE family (one point per family, addressing within-family pseudoreplication), real vs. mode-2 simulated.")
```

Saved file name: corr_identity_integrity_family_level.csv

## 6. Combined summary table

```{r, corr_master_table, echo=FALSE}
master_summary <- dplyr::bind_rows(corr_summary, mode1_summary)

write.csv(master_summary, paste0(OUT, "corr_identity_integrity_master_summary.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
kable(master_summary, digits = 3,
      caption = "Master summary: Pearson/Spearman correlation between TE loci divergence and integrity across all 5 validation genomes (real vs. mode-2 simulated, per-locus; Analysis 1) and the mode-1 'by construction ~0' baseline (pooled and per identity-SD scenario; Analysis 2). A nominal mode-0 baseline was considered but excluded (Section 4) because the available mode-0 runs had reused a mode-2-derived TE mutagenesis table rather than mode 0's own independent draw; mode 1 is representative of both modes 0 and 1's sampling design.")
```

Saved file name: corr_identity_integrity_master_summary.csv

The corresponding supplementary figures are the per-species real-vs-mode-2 plots (Section 3.1)
and the per-scenario mode-1 plots (Section 4.1), shown as separate panels per species/scenario
rather than one combined multi-facet figure - a combined overview was tried first but discarded
because a single shared fill scale across genomes differing by orders of magnitude in TE loci
count (tair10 ~2x10^4 vs. danio ~4x10^6) made all but the largest genome's panel unreadable.
